title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
text: package contains collection data sets designed accompany book Forecasting Exponential Smoothing: State Space Approach Rob J. Hyndman, Anne B. Koehler, J. Keith Ord, Ralph D. Snyder (Springer, 2008).  expsmooth package loaded, forecast package also loaded, providing functions fit forecast exponential smoothing state space models. also use ggplot2 patchwork graphs. vignette follows analysis Section 2.8 book, provides worked solutions Exercises 2.3 2.4. forecast package updated since book published, resulting models estimates differ book. Figure numbers taken book.

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
text: Chapters 1 2 use four data sets included expsmooth package. bonds: 125 monthly US government bond yields (percent per annum) January 1994 May 2004. usnetelec: 55 observations annual US net electricity generation (billion kWh) 1949 2003. ukcars: 113 quarterly observations passenger motor vehicle production UK (thousands cars) first quarter 1977 first quarter 2005. visitors: 240 monthly observations number short-term overseas visitors Australia May 1985 April 2005. time series shown Figure 1.1, reproduced .
code: plot_bonds <- autoplot(bonds) +   labs(     title = "(a) US 10-year bond yields",     x = "Year",     y = "Percentage per annum"   ) plot_usnetelec <- autoplot(usnetelec) +   labs(     title = "(b) US net electricity generation",     x = "Year",     y = "Billion kWh"   ) plot_ukcars <- autoplot(ukcars) +   labs(     title = "(c) UK passenger vehicle production",     x = "Year",     y = "Thousands of cars"   ) plot_visitors <- autoplot(visitors) +   labs(     title = "(d) Overseas visitors to Australia",     x = "Year",     y = "Thousands of people"   ) (plot_bonds | plot_usnetelec) /   (plot_ukcars | plot_visitors)

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
text: part vignette follows automatic forecasting procedure described Section 2.8 book. book selected ETS(,Ad,N) bonds, ETS(M,Md,N) usnetelec, ETS(,N,) ukcars ETS(M,,M) visitors. current version forecast package selects models bonds, ukcars visitors, selects ETS(M,,N) usnetelec. estimation model selection performed ets() function forecasting done forecast() function. part forecast package. basic introduction using functions given Sections 7.6 7.7 Forecasting: Principles Practice Rob J Hyndman George Athanasopoulos. automatic forecasting process carried four data sets. process explained first data set, main results reported others.

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
text: ets() function fits appropriate models (optimising parameters case), selects best model according AICc. AICc default information criterion; AIC BIC can used instead via ic argument. (book used AIC; four series AIC AICc select models.) autoplot() function can used show observed series together estimated level slope components time.  forecast() function used produce point forecasts prediction intervals. summary() function called forecast object, prints model information along point forecasts prediction intervals. autoplot() function can called forecast object produce graph shown Figure 2.1.

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
text: remaining series, show fitted model graph forecasts.
code: fit_usnetelec <- ets(usnetelec) fit_usnetelec #> ETS(M,A,N)  #>  #> Call: #> ets(y = usnetelec) #>  #>   Smoothing parameters: #>     alpha = 0.9999  #>     beta  = 0.2191  #>  #>   Initial states: #>     l = 254.9338  #>     b = 38.3125  #>  #>   sigma:  0.0259 #>  #>      AIC     AICc      BIC  #> 634.0437 635.2682 644.0803 forecast_usnetelec <- forecast(fit_usnetelec, level = 80) autoplot(forecast_usnetelec) +   labs(     title = "US net electricity generation",     x = "Year",     y = "Billion kWh",     caption = "Fig. 2.1b"   )

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
code: fit_ukcars <- ets(ukcars) fit_ukcars #> ETS(A,N,A)  #>  #> Call: #> ets(y = ukcars) #>  #>   Smoothing parameters: #>     alpha = 0.6199  #>     gamma = 1e-04  #>  #>   Initial states: #>     l = 314.2568  #>     s = -1.7579 -44.9601 21.1956 25.5223 #>  #>   sigma:  25.9302 #>  #>      AIC     AICc      BIC  #> 1277.752 1278.819 1296.844 forecast_ukcars <- forecast(fit_ukcars, level = 80) autoplot(forecast_ukcars) +   labs(     title = "UK passenger motor vehicle production",     x = "Year",     y = "Thousands of cars",     caption = "Fig. 2.1c"   )

title: Using expsmooth: worked examples
code: fit_visitors <- ets(visitors) fit_visitors #> ETS(M,A,M)  #>  #> Call: #> ets(y = visitors) #>  #>   Smoothing parameters: #>     alpha = 0.6146  #>     beta  = 2e-04  #>     gamma = 0.192  #>  #>   Initial states: #>     l = 92.9631  #>     b = 2.2221  #>     s = 0.9378 1.0666 1.0669 0.9625 1.3768 1.113 #>            1.0012 0.8219 0.9317 1.0046 0.8755 0.8413 #>  #>   sigma:  0.0536 #>  #>      AIC     AICc      BIC  #> 2603.654 2606.411 2662.825 forecast_visitors <- forecast(fit_visitors, level = 80) autoplot(forecast_visitors) +   labs(     title = "Overseas visitors to Australia",     x = "Year",     y = "Thousands of people",     caption = "Fig. 2.1d"   )
